recent_commits.message: Fixes for #506 and #523: output search limit, sandbox folders, writes beside the script, SPSS encoding (0.4.1.3)
recent_commits.body:
- reproducibility_check searches only the first 20,000 lines of a script's
  printed output for statistical results (option
  metacheck.repro_output_max_lines) and says so in the report (#523, item 2).
  On the SURF server sq8y6's script was stopped after 300 s as it should be,
  but the search through its printed output then kept the job busy until the
  60-minute job limit.
- Docker sandbox: R's cache, configuration and data folders are put in /tmp
  (the home folder is read-only, so renv::restore() stopped), and
  RSTUDIO_PANDOC points to the Pandoc Quarto has in the image (#523, items 4
  and 5).
- Package layout: a quoted relative path whose folder exists from the
  script's own or .Rproj folder, but not from the top, is rewritten to its
  path from the top, so writes beside the script work and later scripts find
  the file (#523, item 3).
- codebook_check: mapply(USE.NAMES = FALSE), so an NA variable name no longer
  stops it with "row names contain missing values" (#523, item 1).
- .sav files with Windows (CP1252) text are read again as CP1252 (#523,
  item 6).
- dryad_info(cache = TRUE) does not reuse listings stored before the paging
  fix of 0.3.3.1, or marked incomplete (#506).

recent_commits.message: Add functions for PsyArXiv's own API (psyarxiv_*)
recent_commits.body:
PsyArXiv now has its own read-only API (https://next.psyarxiv.org/api,
no key). New functions next to the OSF route, which is unchanged:
psyarxiv_search() (full-text search, filters, paging), psyarxiv_info()
(full records: data/prereg/materials statements, COI, supplements
project, file links), psyarxiv_versions(), psyarxiv_author(),
psyarxiv_download(), psyarxiv_dumps()/psyarxiv_dump() (yearly bulk
files), psyarxiv_subjects(), psyarxiv_licenses(). Ids are OSF guids;
links and PsyArXiv DOIs are accepted. The address is the option
metacheck.psyarxiv.api. Tests use recorded answers in
apis/next.psyarxiv.org; downloads are tested live (skipped on CRAN).

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,tables): guard the new running-head and furniture-number rules against real content
recent_commits.body:
Independent review of normalization 1.9.75 / table extraction 2.4.25 found inputs on which each rule
took content for furniture; each is now a test (tests/test_running_head_and_furniture_guards.py).

- Running heads: page numbers folded off a head must be distinct and rise with the page ("Study 1" /
  "Study 2" are headings); a line carrying a statistic or comparison is never taken; the alternating
  rule needs three pages after page 1 and reads parity from the pages present; nothing is stripped
  on page 1, where a line equal to the head is the title.
- Furniture numbers: only the grid's single bare ASCII page number in its first or last row; an axis
  column needs most ticks alone in their row, so years or a Likert key beside labels stay data.
- Public repo: cite consumer requests by date, not by correspondence message id; the hygiene test
  now detects that id shape.

Census on the final rules: 225 papers, 117 changed, every removed line a running head/footer or
download stamp; 125 papers, 66 uncaptioned candidates set aside in 11, all furniture.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.body:
.report_pandoc_dir() looked only in <quarto>/bin/tools/, where Quarto keeps
Pandoc on Windows and macOS. On Linux it is in bin/tools/x86_64/ or
bin/tools/aarch64/, so the checklist, simple and brief reports failed on a
Linux server without a separate Pandoc. Checked on the TU/e Shiny server
(Quarto 1.6.40): before NULL, now bin/tools/x86_64.

recent_commits.body:
PsyArXiv now has its own read-only API (https://next.psyarxiv.org/api,
no key). New functions next to the OSF route, which is unchanged:
psyarxiv_search() (full-text search, filters, paging), psyarxiv_info()
(full records: data/prereg/materials statements, COI, supplements
project, file links), psyarxiv_versions(), psyarxiv_author(),
psyarxiv_download(), psyarxiv_dumps()/psyarxiv_dump() (yearly bulk
files), psyarxiv_subjects(), psyarxiv_licenses(). Ids are OSF guids;
links and PsyArXiv DOIs are accepted. The address is the option
metacheck.psyarxiv.api. Tests use recorded answers in
apis/next.psyarxiv.org; downloads are tested live (skipped on CRAN).

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,tables): guard the new running-head and furniture-number rules against real content
recent_commits.body:
Independent review of normalization 1.9.75 / table extraction 2.4.25 found inputs on which each rule
took content for furniture; each is now a test (tests/test_running_head_and_furniture_guards.py).

- Running heads: page numbers folded off a head must be distinct and rise with the page ("Study 1" /
  "Study 2" are headings); a line carrying a statistic or comparison is never taken; the alternating
  rule needs three pages after page 1 and reads parity from the pages present; nothing is stripped
  on page 1, where a line equal to the head is the title.
- Furniture numbers: only the grid's single bare ASCII page number in its first or last row; an axis
  column needs most ticks alone in their row, so years or a Likert key beside labels stay data.
- Public repo: cite consumer requests by date, not by correspondence message id; the hygiene test
  now detects that id shape.

Census on the final rules: 225 papers, 117 changed, every removed line a running head/footer or
download stamp; 125 papers, 66 uncaptioned candidates set aside in 11, all furniture.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,tables): strip alternating and folio-fused running heads at page edges; a page number or axis scale no longer keeps a duplicate table candidate
recent_commits.body:
Normalization 1.9.75: a second running-head detector compares the extreme line with its page number removed and accepts recto/verso heads (>= 3/4 of one parity's pages). Lines it finds are removed only within the first or last three lines of a page; the exact-repeat rule is unchanged. Measured on 10.1177/0956797610361706 (both heads reached the body).

Table extraction 2.4.25: in the duplicate-of-page-text check for uncaptioned candidates, a bare page number at its page's edge and a decreasing evenly spaced numeric column (a y-axis) no longer count as statistics. Rising runs (item numbering, 10.1098/rsos.250979 p14) still count.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.body:

test that fails on 381f746:
- dropped_glyphs: frames must agree on sampled text lines; a dash glued on its left to a digit,
  letter or closing bracket is an operator/range; the number must occur once at a token start;
  repaired cells carry "restored": "sign" (Cell gains an optional key).
- bottom_extend: an appended value must overlap the printed content of its column (a panel with
  its own column layout is not appended). Census: 45 firings / 32 papers (was 46 / 33).
- flatten: fewer than two folded top-row labels keeps the previous grouping instead of none.
- extract_structured: the picker's _appended_cells key is removed from every table.

CI-window brace false positive (1 brace pair in the 101 PDFs, a set, kept).

restorations. Targeted table/normalization modules: 1660 passed (+ contract test updated).

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.154 - tables reach their last row, keep math-font minus signs, split side-by-side tables, bind columns to spanning group headers
recent_commits.body:
Table extraction 2.4.24, normalization 1.9.74.

- bottom_extend: a Camelot stream grid that stopped above an indented sub-block or label-only row
  gets the rows of values below it, re-read with its own columns; kept only if the original rows
  come back identical (d-15267e, d-f22409, d-d2e9d8 Table 9). Region grids extended this way never
  displace a more complete page grid on the appended rows alone.
- dropped_glyphs: a minus drawn in a TeX/MathTime symbol font, missing from Camelot's text lines,
  is restored from the page text layer (57 cells, 4 manifest papers; rsos.140072 T3, sf/soaf022).
- side-by-side caption labels found when the PDF draws space glyphs; a label must begin its block
  and match the caption's own line (d-d4b785: s12916-023-03146-5 Tables 1/2).
- flatten: only top-row standalone labels start an arm; centred arms end where roles repeat
  (d-bc33a3); super-header stub prose no longer drops the labels (collabra.74820 T2);
  fields.p_text and fields.CI_kind.
- caption trimmer: four-line regions stop at header lines (d-5410ed).
- A4 braces only after CI wording (d-a6101d); H0b joins a split letter-spaced label on one
  baseline (d-091f68); W0t kept-fragment licence guard (d-d68442).
- quality: control characters and operator-less statistics (d-ac50fc).

Measured: 101-PDF manifest render diff vs v2.4.153 (21 papers change, 0 numbers lost except
sign restorations); full suite on the pre-guard snapshot 3819 passed / 6 failed (all six addressed:
brace tests, docs versions, sdist untracked), final-code targeted re-run 1645 passed.

recent_commits.body:

- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"

- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Fixes for #506 and #523: output search limit, sandbox folders, writes beside the script, SPSS encoding (0.4.1.3)
recent_commits.body:
- reproducibility_check searches only the first 20,000 lines of a script's
  printed output for statistical results (option
  metacheck.repro_output_max_lines) and says so in the report (#523, item 2).
  On the SURF server sq8y6's script was stopped after 300 s as it should be,
  but the search through its printed output then kept the job busy until the
  60-minute job limit.
- Docker sandbox: R's cache, configuration and data folders are put in /tmp
  (the home folder is read-only, so renv::restore() stopped), and
  RSTUDIO_PANDOC points to the Pandoc Quarto has in the image (#523, items 4
  and 5).
- Package layout: a quoted relative path whose folder exists from the
  script's own or .Rproj folder, but not from the top, is rewritten to its
  path from the top, so writes beside the script work and later scripts find
  the file (#523, item 3).
- codebook_check: mapply(USE.NAMES = FALSE), so an NA variable name no longer
  stops it with "row names contain missing values" (#523, item 1).
- .sav files with Windows (CP1252) text are read again as CP1252 (#523,
  item 6).
- dryad_info(cache = TRUE) does not reuse listings stored before the paging
  fix of 0.3.3.1, or marked incomplete (#506).

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.153 - W0o compound hyphens, table-text duplicate yields to its grid, flattened CI level is the table's own
recent_commits.body:
normalization 1.9.73, table extraction 2.4.23. Corpus (101 manifest PDFs): 313 hyphen restorations,
64 duplicate markers in 30 papers with 0 numbers lost, 69 of 10,713 flattened rows change level.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(tests,docs): v2.4.153 suite follow-ups - citation version, Well-Being heading, flatten helper passes level context
recent_commits.body:
Full suite on eccd3fa: 5 failed / 3796 passed. Two timing tests failed under machine load and pass
alone (5.8 s). CITATION.cff and README cited 2.4.152. The ip_feldman heading test asserted the
dehyphenated "WellBeing" that W0o now restores to the printed "Well-Being". The blank-header test
helper copies flatten_table's row loop but did not pass level_context, so its caption
"d or dz [95% CI]" never reached _interval_level; production passes it (flatten.py:2040).
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.153 - W0o compound hyphens, table-text duplicate yields to its grid, flattened CI level is the table's own
recent_commits.body:
normalization 1.9.73, table extraction 2.4.23. Corpus (101 manifest PDFs): 313 hyphen restorations,
64 duplicate markers in 30 papers with 0 numbers lost, 69 of 10,713 flattened rows change level.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.body:
Full suite on eccd3fa: 5 failed / 3796 passed. Two timing tests failed under machine load and pass
alone (5.8 s). CITATION.cff and README cited 2.4.152. The ip_feldman heading test asserted the
dehyphenated "WellBeing" that W0o now restores to the printed "Well-Being". The blank-header test

recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.153 - W0o compound hyphens, table-text duplicate yields to its grid, flattened CI level is the table's own
recent_commits.body:
normalization 1.9.73, table extraction 2.4.23. Corpus (101 manifest PDFs): 313 hyphen restorations,
64 duplicate markers in 30 papers with 0 numbers lost, 69 of 10,713 flattened rows change level.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
The workflow pasted the commit message into a single-quoted shell string,
so an apostrophe ("main's") ended the string and the step failed, and the
rest of the message was run as shell code. The message now reaches the
shell as an environment variable and jq writes the JSON; curl --fail makes
a refused webhook show as a failed step.

recent_commits.message: code_read() stops on an HTTP error again instead of reading the error page as code (0.4.0.11)
recent_commits.body:
The new code_read() (#513) fetches a URL with curl::curl_fetch_memory(),
which does not fail on an HTTP error, so a missing file's error page was
read as its code: a github.com 404 gave 682 lines of HTML. readLines() used
to stop there, and code_check recorded the file as not read. code_read()
now stops with "cannot open URL '<url>': HTTP status was <n>" for a status
of 400 or above. The manifest test in test-module-code_check.R no longer
expects the warning readLines() used to give.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.body:
A file modules/<name>.R in the working directory replaced the installed
module <name>, so a server running a check from inside an uploaded folder ran
the upload's code. Built-in modules, then installed ones, then the working
directory and its modules/ folder. Fixes #512.

recent_commits.message: code_read() no longer crashes R on an undefined byte (0.4.0.9)
recent_commits.body:
readr::read_lines() in the guessed encoding crashed R (vroom segfault while
unwinding from "Invalid multibyte sequence") on a byte that encoding leaves
undefined, such as 0x81 in windows-1252. code_read() now reads the bytes and
converts them with iconv(sub = "byte"), in the same guessed encoding. Fixes #511.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Package layout: rewrite only paths that cannot work, writes stay in place (0.4.0.8)
recent_commits.body:
- A relative path that names no file from the top or from the script's
  folder is left as written (code joins it with a folder of its own; the
  rewrite doubled it: processed_data/fig7/processed_data/fig7/x.csv). A path
  relative to the script's folder goes to the file's path from the top; an
  absolute path or one out of the package is rewritten by file name.
- Writes stay where the code puts them, so later scripts find the files;
  only writes to absolute paths or out of the package go to output/.
- The copied files and folders are writable, so a script can save over a
  file the package holds (the Docker sandbox runs as another user).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check runs a local folder's code in a copy of the package (0.4.0.7)
recent_commits.body:
- New argument layout: "package" copies every file to its own path, so code
  that reads folders or imports its own modules finds them; only a path that
  does not work there is rewritten, a path that works is left as written.
  "auto" (default) uses it for a local folder (local_path), and the Psych-DS
  layout otherwise, as before. Each script is written to, and each file
  copied from, its own path, so files with the same name no longer collide.
- A Python file other files import is not run as a script of its own
  (outcome run_by_import), like an R script another script source()s.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Checklist report; Python advice in code_check; OSF token and ResearchBox downloads fixed (0.4.0.6)
recent_commits.body:
- report_type("checklist"): a fifth report type that sorts every check of
  every module into to fix, to improve, decide by hand, for information,
  fine and not applicable, with what was found and what to do on separate
  lines, in the colours and font of metacheck's website. A module can give
  its checks as a `checks` data frame (plus `intro` and `logo`); others are
  shown as one check. New R/report-checklist.R and
  inst/templates/_report_checklist.Rmd; the module "How It Works" text moves
  to .report_how_it_works(); collapse_section() folds in this report type.
- A static table cell starting like a list item ("1. GENERAL INFORMATION")
  no longer opens a list that swallows the rest of the report.
- code_check gives Python code Python advice on package versions
  (requirements.txt and similar are found; .code_env_pinned()).
- OSF downloads with an OSF token no longer send the token to the storage
  host, and work again since the OSF moved to Oracle storage (#508).
- ResearchBox downloads send the new text file ids.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Divide whole numbers with plain floor() and ceiling()
recent_commits.body:
* floor_div() and ceiling_div() checked floor(a / b) by multiplying it back out. Below 2^53, IEEE 754 division already makes floor(a / b) exact for whole numbers, so the check never fired. Above 2^53 the products round too, and in a random sample of 200,000 cases the check broke correct results about 14 times as often as it repaired wrong ones.

* Every call site now uses floor() or ceiling() directly; the reasoning is in the comment at the top of R/unround.R.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give a value that would look like a bound just enough places
recent_commits.body:
* format_number() fell back to 12 significant digits for a value that
would look whole or like a bound, e.g. 0.146504464074. It now adds the
fewest decimal places that set the value apart, e.g. 0.146504.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

items had to be a positive whole number, but was 1.

recent_commits.message: Don't show DEBIT's example SD as an excluded bound
recent_commits.body:
* Picking the k closest to the middle of the range didn't help when only
one k passes: debit_explain(0, sd = 0.147, n = 320, digits_x = 1,
digits_sd = 3, rounding = "down") showed an SD of 0.1465 as in a range
above 0.1465. format_number() now takes the bounds a value is compared
to and shows it in more detail if it would look like one of them.

behind binary_sd_attainable() to both it and binary_ones_shown().

"scale range" instead of "test 1", and grimmer_explain() said the
ceiling was "too small" rather than that the range was empty.

recent_commits.message: Show rounding bounds in full at 4+ decimal places

with 4 or more decimals were cut off, and describe_range() could then
call an interval a single point. It now shows `digits + 2` places, at
least four.

bounds undefined" reasons to explain_undecidable() rather than letting
them reach the candidate loop with an NA verdict.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges

Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus

recent_commits.message: fix(tests,docs): v2.4.153 suite follow-ups - citation version, Well-Being heading, flatten helper passes level context
recent_commits.body:
Full suite on eccd3fa: 5 failed / 3796 passed. Two timing tests failed under machine load and pass
alone (5.8 s). CITATION.cff and README cited 2.4.152. The ip_feldman heading test asserted the
dehyphenated "WellBeing" that W0o now restores to the printed "Well-Being". The blank-header test
helper copies flatten_table's row loop but did not pass level_context, so its caption
"d or dz [95% CI]" never reached _interval_level; production passes it (flatten.py:2040).
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.153 - W0o compound hyphens, table-text duplicate yields to its grid, flattened CI level is the table's own
recent_commits.body:
normalization 1.9.73, table extraction 2.4.23. Corpus (101 manifest PDFs): 313 hyphen restorations,
64 duplicate markers in 30 papers with 0 numbers lost, 69 of 10,713 flattened rows change level.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: report() saves the report on another disk too (0.4.0.5)
recent_commits.body:
report() renders in R's temporary folder and moved the result with
file.rename(), which cannot move a file to another disk: it returns
FALSE without an error, so the output file kept the "test" that
report() writes to check the path. On the SURF API, whose job folders
are on a storage volume, an installed module's report came back as
"test". .report_move() copies the file when renaming fails, and stops
with an error when that fails too.
recent_commits.author: Lakens
