recent_commits.message: Convert PDFs on SURF by default; data_check reads every same-named file; code_check names local files (0.4.0.4)
recent_commits.body:
- convert_bibr() gets backend = "surf" (metacheck's API on SURF Research
  Cloud, no key needed), used by "auto" unless a Scienceverse key or a bibr
  address is given; SURF_API_URL sets its address. The server's reason is
  passed on when a conversion fails, DOC/DOCX are refused before sending,
  and the file name the server reports (input.pdf) is replaced by the real
  one. convert() asks SURF first (checked with .surf_isalive()), then falls
  back to the old order.
- data_check kept each table under its file name alone, so same-named files
  in different folders replaced each other (4 of 46 tables checked in a
  measurement package). Files now get a unique source_file
  (.data_source_keys()): the name, else the path, else repository + path;
  previews, columns, findings and codebook_check's labels use it.
- code_check's report table showed NA for the names of local files (a link
  to a missing web address); it now shows their path.
- Help pages regenerated (three were out of date with their source).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Show everything in the file tree; classify licences, models, .vcd, .pgf and package lists (0.4.0.3)
recent_commits.body:
- File tree: a local folder is listed itself, with hidden files, junk files
  and empty folders; a repository link also shows repo_check's junk files.
  Marks: "junk: remove", "junk: keep only on purpose" (a junk folder is one
  line with its number of files), "hidden file", "empty folder". Folders,
  empty ones included, before files. The tree sits in a scroll box, and the
  repository apps show it open instead of folded. data_check passes
  repo_check's useless_files to it.
- Classifier: LICENSE/LICENCE/COPYING without extension -> documentation
  (licence role); .slx and .mph -> code; .vcd -> data; .pgf -> output;
  requirements*.txt and Pipfile -> code
- .mc_request() moved above .batch_query()'s roxygen block, so it no longer
  takes over that help page
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: repo_check flags junk files as TU/e's data managers do; share the file tree (0.4.0.2)
recent_commits.body:
- .useless_file_kind() adds the junk rules of TU/e's data managers: editor
  backups (file~, .bak, .swp, .swo), temporary files (.tmp, .temp),
  .Rhistory, .TemporaryItems and every ~$ lock file as problems; version
  control (.git, .svn, .hg) and editor settings (.idea, .vscode) as
  suggestions (.useless_file_severity())
- repo_check: a problem kind turns the light red, a suggestion kind yellow;
  the files are returned as useless_files (paper_id, repo_url, file_path,
  kind, severity), and the report says which to remove and which to keep
  only on purpose
- local_files() lists hidden files of these kinds (.DS_Store, .Rhistory,
  .git/), so repo_check finds them in a local folder too
- R/file-tree.R: data_check's file tree (.file_tree_rows(),
  .file_tree_block()) moved into the package, with .file_tree() for the
  repository apps' brief report and external modules; the apps no longer
  keep their own copy
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Install modules from GitHub with module_install() (0.4.0.1)
recent_commits.body:
- module_install("owner/repo", ref) downloads a repository into the
  metacheck user data folder (or METACHECK_MODULES_DIR); every .R file
  with a roxygen header in its top folder or modules/ becomes a module
  that module_run(), report(), module_info() and module_help() find by
  name. Nothing is saved when a name is already used by a built-in
  module, another installed repository, or twice in the same repository.
  A module can state its lowest metacheck version (#' @metacheck x.y.z),
  checked by module_install() and module_run().
- module_update(), module_remove() and module_installed()
- module_list() lists installed modules, with their repository in a new
  source column; module_list(external = FALSE) lists built-in ones only
- report: an installed module's How It Works names its repository and
  commit instead of linking to a manual chapter
- test-module-repo_check.R: the three summary tables include the
  repo_unchecked column added in c5c98a1
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.author: brandmaier

recent_commits.message: Give a value that would look like a bound just enough places
recent_commits.body:
* format_number() fell back to 12 significant digits for a value that
would look whole or like a bound, e.g. 0.146504464074. It now adds the
fewest decimal places that set the value apart, e.g. 0.146504.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that explain_map()'s data was tested with formula = "mean_n"
recent_commits.body:
* Through explain_map(), debit_explain()'s own check said `formula` is
"mean_n", though the user never passed `formula`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make unexplainable GRIMMER reasons an internal error
recent_commits.body:
* "GRIM undecidable" and "SD rounding bounds undefined" can't happen,
and explain_undecidable() has no words for them: it said the number of
items had to be a positive whole number, but was 1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't show DEBIT's example SD as an excluded bound
recent_commits.body:
* Picking the k closest to the middle of the range didn't help when only
one k passes: debit_explain(0, sd = 0.147, n = 320, digits_x = 1,
digits_sd = 3, rounding = "down") showed an SD of 0.1465 as in a range
above 0.1465. format_number() now takes the bounds a value is compared
to and shows it in more detail if it would look like one of them.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Share explanation helpers with the tests they explain
recent_commits.body:
* spread_out_most() gives the values behind sum_squares_scale_max() to
both it and describe_spread_out(), and binary_spread_root() the root
behind binary_sd_attainable() to both it and binary_ones_shown().
* debit_explain() gets a `formula` argument that rejects "mean_n", so
explain_map() no longer has to know what the explainer can't do.
* Align the pipes in the mapper-tier test.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't blame the scale for a GRIMMER range that was already empty
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_candidate() applied the scale ceiling even when the sum of
squares range held no whole number without it, so the reason became
"scale range" instead of "test 1", and grimmer_explain() said the
ceiling was "too small" rather than that the range was empty.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show rounding bounds in full at 4+ decimal places
recent_commits.body:
* format_number() rounded to 4 places, so the bounds of a value reported
with 4 or more decimals were cut off, and describe_range() could then
call an interval a single point. It now shows `digits + 2` places, at
least four.
* grimmer_explain() routes the "GRIM undecidable" and "SD rounding
bounds undefined" reasons to explain_undecidable() rather than letting
them reach the candidate loop with an NA verdict.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let explain_map() dispatch on any class
recent_commits.body:
* The class check ran in the generic ahead of `UseMethod()`, so no method
for another class could ever be reached. It is `explain_map.default()` now,
with the same error, and `explain_print()` only checks for a tibble before
slicing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pass explain_map() rows as plain vectors
recent_commits.body:
* `explain_row()` subset the tibble with `data[i, cols]` per row. It now
indexes a list of the columns, which saves about 6% on a 932-row
`grim_map_seq()` output; the rest is the `*_explain()` calls themselves.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write GRIMMER explanations only for candidates that are shown
recent_commits.body:
* The loop built a paragraph for every failing candidate sum and then kept
the first three. It now counts the failures after the third without writing
them out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Share DEBIT's bounds with debit_explain() and stop listing every k
recent_commits.body:
* `debit_bounds()` clamps the mean's and the SD's rounding bounds once, for
`debit_scalar()` and `debit_explain()` alike, so the text can't drift from
the bounds that decided the test.
* `debit_explain()` listed every number of ones from `sum_lower` to
`sum_upper`, millions for a large `n`. `binary_ones_shown()` finds the few
the text needs next to the roots of `k * (n - k) = spread`; a brute-force test
checks it against the full list.
* The example `k` is now the passing one whose SD is closest to the middle of
the range. The smallest one sat at a bound, and once rounded for display, its
SD could read as exactly the bound the text had just excluded.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write out large numbers in explanations
recent_commits.body:
* `paste()` wrote round numbers like 100000 as 1e+05 in the text and in the
header. Each `*_explain()` function now raises `scipen` while it runs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain a missing `items` value instead of erroring
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_explain()` and `grimmer_explain()` tested `items != 1` for the
header, which failed on `NA`, so one such row aborted `explain_map()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pick explain_print() rows like dplyr::slice() and check for mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print(data, ...) passes the dots to dplyr::slice() instead of
  taking `n`, so any rows can be printed, not just the first ones.
* explain_map() and explain_print() call check_explainable(), which
  requires output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() (or
  their sequence and total-n mappers) instead of failing in dispatch.
* The re-test error names the row by its values, not by a position that
  slice() or filter() had already shifted.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
recent_commits.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: repo_check flags junk files as TU/e's data managers do; share the file tree (0.4.0.2)
recent_commits.body:
- .useless_file_kind() adds the junk rules of TU/e's data managers: editor
  backups (file~, .bak, .swp, .swo), temporary files (.tmp, .temp),
  .Rhistory, .TemporaryItems and every ~$ lock file as problems; version
  control (.git, .svn, .hg) and editor settings (.idea, .vscode) as
  suggestions (.useless_file_severity())
- repo_check: a problem kind turns the light red, a suggestion kind yellow;
  the files are returned as useless_files (paper_id, repo_url, file_path,
  kind, severity), and the report says which to remove and which to keep
  only on purpose
- local_files() lists hidden files of these kinds (.DS_Store, .Rhistory,
  .git/), so repo_check finds them in a local folder too
- R/file-tree.R: data_check's file tree (.file_tree_rows(),
  .file_tree_block()) moved into the package, with .file_tree() for the
  repository apps' brief report and external modules; the apps no longer
  keep their own copy
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Install modules from GitHub with module_install() (0.4.0.1)
recent_commits.body:
- module_install("owner/repo", ref) downloads a repository into the
  metacheck user data folder (or METACHECK_MODULES_DIR); every .R file
  with a roxygen header in its top folder or modules/ becomes a module
  that module_run(), report(), module_info() and module_help() find by
  name. Nothing is saved when a name is already used by a built-in
  module, another installed repository, or twice in the same repository.
  A module can state its lowest metacheck version (#' @metacheck x.y.z),
  checked by module_install() and module_run().
- module_update(), module_remove() and module_installed()
- module_list() lists installed modules, with their repository in a new
  source column; module_list(external = FALSE) lists built-in ones only
- report: an installed module's How It Works names its repository and
  commit instead of linking to a manual chapter
- test-module-repo_check.R: the three summary tables include the
  repo_unchecked column added in c5c98a1
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Show a reproducibility check that ran code in the brief report, also when green (0.3.3.19)
recent_commits.body:
report_qmd() kept only red/yellow/fail modules in brief mode, so a

reproducibility_check does when it ran at least one script (#504).

recent_commits.message: Redirect script writes to output/ relative to the sandbox root, so they work in Docker (0.3.3.18)
recent_commits.body:
repro_write_scripts() replaced {{REPRO_OUTPUT}} with file.path(root,
"output"), an absolute host path; the Docker sandbox mounts root at
/sandbox, so every script that wrote a file failed inside the container.
The replacement is now "output/", which works in both sandboxes since
every script runs with the sandbox root as working directory (#502).
New tests: the rewritten path is relative, and a script writing a file
runs in a Docker container and its file reaches the host's output/.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Redirect sandbox writes to a relative output/ path, so they work in the Docker sandbox (0.3.3.18)
recent_commits.body:
repro_write_scripts() redirected write calls to file.path(root, "output"),
a host path that does not exist inside the Docker sandbox (root is mounted
at /sandbox), so every script that writes a file failed there after its
analysis had run. Every run uses root as its working directory in both
sandboxes, so the relative path output/<name> is right in both (#502).

recent_commits.message: Report OSF links that could not be checked; name uploaded zips by their folder in the repository check app (0.3.3.17)
recent_commits.body:
- .osf_parse_response() gives each failed lookup a reason in an `error`
  column (HTTP 503 -> osf_type "error", "the OSF API did not answer";
  404/410 "unfound" with their own reason; 429), so it is not cached on disk;
  osf_info() no longer keeps failed lookups in its session cache (#501)
- repo_check keeps OSF links that could not be looked up, with their reason
  in gated_repos, instead of removing them with the registrations (#501)
- repo_check's summary and report name repositories that could not be
  checked instead of counting them as empty or without README (all
  platforms); the light is not green then; new repo_unchecked column
- Repository check app: an uploaded zip is unpacked into a folder named
  after it and checked from the folder above, so the report shows its name,
  not the server's temporary path (#500); new test-app-repocheck.R
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Accept .NET multipart uploads in the plumber API; refuse JSON that is not bibr output (0.3.3.16)
recent_commits.body:
- plumber API: parse_upload() reads the request body with
  webutils::parse_http() (plumber's own parser) instead of
  mime::parse_multipart(), which only recognised a part whose
  Content-Disposition header came first; .NET's MultipartFormDataContent
  (PowerShell, C#) writes Content-Type first, so its uploads and form fields
  were lost. Same returned shape, endpoints unchanged (#498)
- .read_bibr() stops with "is not bibr output (it has no paper_id)" for a
  JSON file without a paper_id; read() skips it with a warning. module_run()
  keeps the module's own error when paper_id() fails in its handler (#499)
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Give repository requests a stall guard; ask zip_peek for the exact central directory (0.3.3.15)
recent_commits.body:
- .mc_request(): httr2::request() with curl's low-speed limit (< 1 KB/s
  for 60 s) and a 30 s connect timeout, used by the 38 repository and
  database requests that had no time limit (zip listing, GitHub, GitLab,
  OSF, ResearchBox (300 s), PsychArchives, DSpace, AsPredicted, FSD,
  DataONE, Dryad, CrossRef, PubPeer, Retraction Watch, RegCheck status,
  paper corpora, prereg_check's schema). Not used for LLM, GROBID, bibr or
  upload requests, whose servers work before answering (#473)
- zip_peek(): after a first tail too short for the central directory, the
  second request asks for the bytes the end record says it needs
  (.parse_zip_central_dir(need_only = TRUE)), up to 64 MB, instead of a
  fixed 1 MB
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Unpack only kept archive files within max_file_size in data_check (0.3.3.14)
recent_commits.body:
- .archive_keep(): the keep rule of .archive_rows() (data, code, README and
  codebook documentation, not skip_types or useless files), applied to an
  archive's listing before anything is unpacked
- .expand_compressed() decompresses a .gz/.bz2/.xz only when the inner file
  is kept, and stops at max_bytes (partial copy deleted); .expand_zip() and
  .expand_tar() unpack only kept members within max_bytes (sizes from the
  zip listing or tar headers; a compressed tar's are checked after
  unpacking). Files over the limit are listed without a copy and added to
  data_check's oversize record; copies over the limit from earlier runs are
  removed (#472)
- .rate_limit_wait test allows a few seconds instead of an exact rounded 900
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: power: free-text categories mapped onto known values, report unchecked paragraphs, require ellmer 0.4.2 (0.3.3.13)
recent_commits.body:
- The LLM answers power_type, statistical_test, effect_size_metric and
  software as free strings; .power_canonicalise() maps them onto the known
  values, keeping an unmatched answer in *_other (new software_other). A
  value outside a type_enum() made Groq reject the whole call (POWSIM)

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Pick explain_print() rows like dplyr::slice() and check for mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print(data, ...) passes the dots to dplyr::slice() instead of
  taking `n`, so any rows can be printed, not just the first ones.
* explain_map() and explain_print() call check_explainable(), which
  requires output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() (or
  their sequence and total-n mappers) instead of failing in dispatch.
* The re-test error names the row by its values, not by a position that
  slice() or filter() had already shifted.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
recent_commits.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized

recent_commits.message: Pick explain_print() rows like dplyr::slice() and check for mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print(data, ...) passes the dots to dplyr::slice() instead of
  taking `n`, so any rows can be printed, not just the first ones.
* explain_map() and explain_print() call check_explainable(), which
  requires output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() (or
  their sequence and total-n mappers) instead of failing in dispatch.
* The re-test error names the row by its values, not by a position that
  slice() or filter() had already shifted.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
recent_commits.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Stop the quadratic rescan of rejected blocks in .r_output_tables() (0.3.3.8)
recent_commits.body:
A printed data frame with no numeric column made every row start a new
scan of the rest of the print, so parsing console output grew with the
square of the rows (384 s for 1,000 rows, hours for 10,000). A rejected
block is now remembered: a later start inside it is only split when its
pattern of non-blank character positions differs from the last block
actually split, the only way its result can differ. Output is identical
on 113 cases; 1,000 rows take about 4 s. A progress line is printed
before each script's output is parsed.

Closes #483
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Pick explain_print() rows like dplyr::slice() and check for mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print(data, ...) passes the dots to dplyr::slice() instead of
  taking `n`, so any rows can be printed, not just the first ones.
* explain_map() and explain_print() call check_explainable(), which
  requires output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() (or
  their sequence and total-n mappers) instead of failing in dispatch.
* The re-test error names the row by its values, not by a position that
  slice() or filter() had already shifted.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
recent_commits.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

scan of the rest of the print, so parsing console output grew with the
square of the rows (384 s for 1,000 rows, hours for 10,000). A rejected
block is now remembered: a later start inside it is only split when its
pattern of non-blank character positions differs from the last block
actually split, the only way its result can differ. Output is identical
on 113 cases; 1,000 rows take about 4 s. A progress line is printed
before each script's output is parsed.

Extends the operating-system file filter to every file software creates by
itself that holds nothing a reader can use: operating-system files (macOS,
Windows, Linux desktops), RStudio's .Rproj.user/, Jupyter checkpoints,
compiled Python files and Office/LibreOffice lock files. Patterns from

that may matter (.RData, .Rhistory, backups, *.tmp, knitr caches) are kept.

them by kind in "Files that do not belong in the repository". The kind is
taken from the last path segment without basename(), which expanded a leading

recent_commits.message: Support LDbase in repo_check; leave out operating-system files; warn on firewall browser checks (0.3.3.4)
recent_commits.body:
LDbase (ldbase.org, FSU's repository for educational and developmental
sciences) has no API, so the new ldbase_links()/ldbase_info() read its public
pages: links to projects, datasets, code and documents and 10.33009 DOIs are
found; a project's whole hierarchy (child projects included) is listed, each
item's current file in a folder named after the item, with the licence of
each item. Files download without an account. Pages are requested at most
once per second. Checked on 10 LDbase projects.

repo_check and data_check leave out files the operating system adds
(__MACOSX/, ._ files, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini) and repo_check lists
them for the authors to remove: in one LDbase zip they were 993 of 1,826
listed files, and the ._ copies of .csv files were read as data.

A host's AWS WAF browser check (HTTP 202 + x-amzn-waf-action: challenge) now
gives a warning once per host; such files used to be skipped without a word
because their size could not be read.

DOIs under 10.33009 are no longer also looked up by dspace7_links();
open_practices counts "LDbase" as a repository word.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Keep one copy of each function defined twice in R/ (0.3.3.7)
recent_commits.body:
Eleven internal functions and one constant were defined twice; R loads R/
alphabetically, so one copy silently replaced the other. Kept: R/stat_helpers.R
for the nine statistics helpers and .STAT_PLACEHOLDERS (the file created as
their single home), omv.R for .html_inline_images(), reproducibility_check.R
for .repro_split_args(). All copies were identical, so behaviour is unchanged.
Each deleted copy leaves a one-line pointer to the kept one. New test fails
when any name is defined twice.

Closes #482
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Stop the quadratic character walks that hung reproducibility_check (0.3.3.6)
recent_commits.body:
Every place that walked text one character at a time with substr(x, i, i)
now splits the text into characters once and indexes the vector. For text
with a non-ASCII character substr() counts from the start on every call, so
the walk was quadratic: 201 s for a 200,000-character script, hours for a
1-MB one. Results are identical on 413 real R and Python scripts.

Changed: .repro_redirect_writes(), .repro_format_call_refs(),
.repro_split_args() (both copies), .repro_content_sniff(),
.r_call_object_ref(), .omv_extract_syntax(), .smcl_render_line().
repro_write_scripts() prints a line per script, so a slow rewrite can be
told apart from a hang.

Closes #481
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Leave out and report all files that do not belong in a repository
recent_commits.body:
Extends the operating-system file filter to every file software creates by
itself that holds nothing a reader can use: operating-system files (macOS,
Windows, Linux desktops), RStudio's .Rproj.user/, Jupyter checkpoints,
compiled Python files and Office/LibreOffice lock files. Patterns from
GitHub's ignore-file templates, each also found in real repositories; files
that may matter (.RData, .Rhistory, backups, *.tmp, knitr caches) are kept.

repo_check and data_check leave them out of the file list; repo_check reports
them by kind in "Files that do not belong in the repository". The kind is
taken from the last path segment without basename(), which expanded a leading
"~" ("~$report.docx" became "Documents$report.docx").
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Support LDbase in repo_check; leave out operating-system files; warn on firewall browser checks (0.3.3.4)
recent_commits.body:
LDbase (ldbase.org, FSU's repository for educational and developmental
sciences) has no API, so the new ldbase_links()/ldbase_info() read its public
pages: links to projects, datasets, code and documents and 10.33009 DOIs are
found; a project's whole hierarchy (child projects included) is listed, each
item's current file in a folder named after the item, with the licence of
each item. Files download without an account. Pages are requested at most
once per second. Checked on 10 LDbase projects.

repo_check and data_check leave out files the operating system adds
(__MACOSX/, ._ files, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini) and repo_check lists
them for the authors to remove: in one LDbase zip they were 993 of 1,826
listed files, and the ._ copies of .csv files were read as data.

A host's AWS WAF browser check (HTTP 202 + x-amzn-waf-action: challenge) now
gives a warning once per host; such files used to be skipped without a word
because their size could not be read.

DOIs under 10.33009 are no longer also looked up by dspace7_links();
open_practices counts "LDbase" as a repository word.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Python support fixes in reproducibility_check, %>% from other scripts, data_check and repo_check fixes (0.3.3.3)
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check (#479):
- Compare reported statistics with the analysis output once, after the R and
  the Python code, so Python output is included; Python-only papers keep the
  SPSS/Stata, self-reproducible-output and other-language sections and the
  SPSS/Stata red light
- Extract the code of Python notebooks and Quarto documents (and R-kernel
  notebooks) before running it
- Check Python syntax with ast.parse(); fall back to python3; report Python
  files as not run, instead of stopping, when no interpreter is found
- Install packages under their pip name (sklearn -> scikit-learn, ...)
- Require callr only for R code; drop the Python NameError re-run
- Return the summary as one text (two made the report error for R + Python)
- Stop exporting .repro_py_defined_vars(); correct help text and comments

R scripts that fail on %>% because packages are loaded in another script:
- A script another script runs with source() is only run inside that script
  (outcome run_by_source)
- Otherwise the re-run adds the library() calls of the project's other
  scripts, else the one package that exports the function, else magrittr;
  recorded in modifications and reported as reproducible after repair

Comparison with the paper: use the output's STATO type when a value's name is
not recognised (scipy's statistic/pvalue); type F_onewayResult,
PearsonRResult and Chi2ContingencyResult

data_check: warn on space-separated .csv files; keep the summary, report and
light when no table is readable (and return the column table as `table`);
read only the header line in the trial-level check (#477)

repo_check: ignore CI/service configuration files when deciding whether a
root-level R package is the deposit (#469)

reproducibility_check(workers > 1): copy all metacheck.* options into each
background process (#474)

check_file_naming(): help no longer lists case rules it does not check

Closes #479
Closes #474
Closes #477
Closes #469

  files as not run, instead of stopping, when no interpreter is found

- Return the summary as one text (two made the report error for R + Python)
- Stop exporting .repro_py_defined_vars(); correct help text and comments

- A script another script runs with source() is only run inside that script
  (outcome run_by_source)

  scripts, else the one package that exports the function, else magrittr;
  recorded in modifications and reported as reproducible after repair

not recognised (scipy's statistic/pvalue); type F_onewayResult,

Closes #474

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as

recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.

recent_commits.message: Drop GRIMMER's test 2 and deprecate grimmer(tolerance)
recent_commits.body:
* Test 1 derives the admissible sums of squares from exact integer bounds that are the inverse of the SD's rounding, so every integer between them rounds back to the reported SD. Test 2 re-rounded each of them anyway, with a floating-point tolerance that could only lose matches.
* The parity test now needs no enumeration: two or more admissible integers include both parities, and a single one is compared to the sum. GRIMMER_CHUNK_SIZE goes with the loop.
* A sweep of 9,000 random cases over every rounding method, symmetric, items, and scale bounds gives the same verdicts and reasons as before. "GRIMMER inconsistent (test 2)" is no longer a possible reason.
* tolerance is deprecated the way grim()'s is.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fetch Dryad zip members by downloading the archive once (#471)
recent_commits.body:
Fetching members by byte range costs two requests per member, which
exhausts Dryad's daily request limit on corpus runs. .zip_fetch_members()
gains a whole-archive mode: when at least 3 members are wanted and the
archive (size estimated from its central directory) fits the budget, it
downloads the archive once, keeps it on disk for restarted runs, and
extracts the wanted members locally; anything not delivered falls back to
the per-member fetch. Enabled only for datadryad.org archives, in
download_repo_files() and code_check's zip expansion. Version 0.3.2.2.

recent_commits.message: Drop GRIMMER's test 2 and deprecate grimmer(tolerance)
recent_commits.body:
* Test 1 derives the admissible sums of squares from exact integer bounds that are the inverse of the SD's rounding, so every integer between them rounds back to the reported SD. Test 2 re-rounded each of them anyway, with a floating-point tolerance that could only lose matches.
* The parity test now needs no enumeration: two or more admissible integers include both parities, and a single one is compared to the sum. GRIMMER_CHUNK_SIZE goes with the loop.
* A sweep of 9,000 random cases over every rounding method, symmetric, items, and scale bounds gives the same verdicts and reasons as before. "GRIMMER inconsistent (test 2)" is no longer a possible reason.
* tolerance is deprecated the way grim()'s is.

recent_commits.body:
Fetching members by byte range costs two requests per member, which
exhausts Dryad's daily request limit on corpus runs. .zip_fetch_members()
gains a whole-archive mode: when at least 3 members are wanted and the
archive (size estimated from its central directory) fits the budget, it
downloads the archive once, keeps it on disk for restarted runs, and
extracts the wanted members locally; anything not delivered falls back to
the per-member fetch. Enabled only for datadryad.org archives, in
download_repo_files() and code_check's zip expansion. Version 0.3.2.2.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add `grim_plot_rates()`
recent_commits.body:
* Plots each study's observed GRIM-inconsistency rate against the rate
  expected for random means, with reference lines at zero and on the
  diagonal; point area is the number of testable value sets.
* Colors points by observed / expected rate, uncapped: a fraction
  above 1 is beyond what random digits produce, which in a study with
  many value sets points to a problem in the analysis.

recent_commits.message: Revise the vignettes for 1.0.0
recent_commits.body:
* `vignette("rounding-in-depth")` misattributed the downward mean of
  `round(seq(4.5, 10.5))` to floating-point error. Those ties are exact;
  the parity rule only preserves the mean if as many ties are rounded
  down as up. The section now separates exact ties at whole numbers
  from the inexact decimal case, and the vignette covers the
  `round_ties_*()` functions, the full IEEE 754 table, and `unround()`
  as the tests actually use it (`digits`, all three tests).
* The GRIM, GRIMMER, and DEBIT vignettes are rewritten in a plainer
  style around the same examples, without `pkgload::load_all()` in the
  setup chunk, and the DEBIT one documents `formula`.
* The in-depth, simple, devtools, and rounding-options vignettes are
  trimmed, and outdated statements corrected: mappers reject non-tibble
  data frames, `n` may come back integer, and `Vectorize()` is not how
  the three tests are vectorized.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Warn that inconsistent percentages often have innocent causes
recent_commits.body:
* A new section of `?is_percentage_of` lists the common ones: a
different denominator, a sample size that changed between analyses,
and other rounding. It points to `is_percentage_of_map_seq(var = "n")`
for finding the denominator that fits.

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Revive the baseline consistency tests for percentages and sums
recent_commits.body:
* `is_percentage_of()` checks whether a reported percentage is what a
reported count out of `n` would be reported as. It reuses GRIM's
`sum_range()`, so it runs in exact integer arithmetic under any rounding
method. `is_percentage_of_map()` and `is_percentage_of_map_seq()` lift it
to the mapper tiers.

* `add_up_to()` checks whether counts sum to their total, returning `NA`
for fractional values, whose sums are not exact. `add_up_to_map()` is
the first mapper built with `function_map(.reported_variadic)` (#42).

* Both get `audit()` methods. `error_digits_missing()` shows an example
call with the percentage test's own arguments.

* Replace the test file that had been commented out since 2023 with an
exact-oracle test, a check against GRIM, and mapper tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

Clopper-Pearson interval around `estimate` from `stats::binom.test()`,
one-sided like the test.

* An invalid `conf.level` is now an error naming `grim_binomial()`.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): two 2.4.152 patterns are linear on a long token
recent_commits.body:

'95% ' prefix (\d+%) were retried from every character of a long token:

starts only at a token's first character, where the leftmost match starts
anyway. Output byte-identical on all 125 corpus papers; 0 mismatches in

recent_commits.body:
Sonnet consult (tier 2, 2026-10-09, tmp/consult/round-wave1-2026-10-09):

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): consult findings on the pagination verdict - glued page tokens count as values; years are not page numbers
recent_commits.body:
Sonnet consult (tier 2, 2026-10-08, tmp/consult/round-pagination-2026-10-08):
1. _value_followed_fraction skipped any verified page-number TOKEN, so a row
   label followed by its count '4' in a 12-page paper read as furniture. Now a

   collabra.369 repeated table note, 1 running header 'Frontiers in Psychology'
   in 10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1138469 - the one visible cost).
3. 4-digit values in 1900-2100 are years as readily as page numbers; excluded

Both reproduced by tests that failed first. Findings 2 (table integers on PDFs
with no page numbers) and the ordinal-path note are logged (d-547465, d-1b2f69).
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): page numbers are decided on the raw text; table values and row labels survive
recent_commits.body:
F3: the page-number strip ran after most form feeds were gone and blanked every
+1 chain of bare integers 20+ lines apart, so table columns chained like pages.
122 random repository PDFs: 2,735 lines blanked, 44 papers over their page count.
Page-verified 10.1016/j.jesp.2010.02.007 p3: it deleted Table 1's raw ratings and
Table 4's ranks. _pagination_verdict decides on the raw text (own-block bare
integer = page index + an offset shared by a run of >=3 near-consecutive pages;
one per page; page-count floor max(form feeds, chars/4000)); the late step blanks
those lines by ordinal, or by neighbour containment when the count drifted. After:
0 papers over; idempotency corpus 23/23 (two-pagination 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.104052).
Unpaginated text keeps the old rule.

F1: the repeated-line once_per_page arm now keeps a line followed by its value
(verified page numbers skipped). 150-PDF census: 102 lines taken, 2 were row
labels (10.1371/journal.pone.0285199), now kept; furniture still removed.

Also: bound the late-join label group added in 4a1471d (unbounded \S+? was
quadratic: test_normalize_scales_sub_quadratically 0.94 s -> 4.79 s).

Canary (ip_feldman_2025_pspb): render diff vs HEAD is 33 lines, all bare
integers - 13 table-text values kept, page numbers 18/19 now removed. The two
ledger findings first keyed on this run (Table 10 -.07, Table 5 row labels)
are byte-identical in the HEAD render: not caused by this change.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(sections): DOCX and HTML normalized_text is normalized; markup headings follow it
recent_commits.body:
Only the PDF branch called normalize_text, so on DOCX/HTML the field named
normalized_text was the raw markup reconstruction (a U+2212 minus reached
consumers as U+2212) and a non-default normalization_level raised. Both branches
now normalize at the requested level (preserve_math_glyphs honoured) and carry
the annotator's BlockHint offsets through a line-level alignment
(sections/_offsets.py: 0.003-0.54 s per real DOCX; a character-level difflib took
up to 349 s). A hint whose whole span normalization deleted is dropped and
recorded (sections_markup_hint_dropped). Consumer-visible: academic level now
spells Greek names in ASCII here as it does for PDFs (etap2), so the DOCX test
asserts that form and the verbatim form under preserve_math_glyphs=True.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): H0 never deletes a banner-shaped line that carries a labelled statistic
recent_commits.body:
Promised to ESCImate 2026-08-22 (their §3): the digit-free assertion belongs on
H0's line deletion, not on the U+0008 strip. The labelled/bracketed/Greek arms
of render._STATISTICAL_CONTENT_RE move to normalize._LABELLED_STATISTIC_PATTERN
and render composes them back (0 verdict differences over 49,442 real lines).
Measured over the 125-paper manifest: H0 drops 313 lines, 0 carry a labelled
statistic, so no current output changes; the broad predicate would have kept
15 mastheads/arXiv stamps, which is why H0 asks the narrower question. A kept
line is recorded as fallback h0_banner_kept_statistic.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): a page boundary rejoined across a split statistic lands before it
recent_commits.body:
keep_break_in_rejoin promised the form feed 'BEFORE the whole token', but the
comma-anchored and operator-anchored late-join sites matched from the previous
token's comma or from the operator, so the boundary landed inside a statistic:
'2.34\f, 95% CI', 'p \f= .031', '95% \fCI 2.046' (census: 5 of 994 boundaries).
Comma sites now emit it after the separator (after=True); the operator site
captures its label, and the CI/OR/RR/HR site its 'NN%' prefix, in the match.
What joins is unchanged; only where the boundary sits.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Fetch Dryad zip members by downloading the archive once (#471)
recent_commits.body:
Fetching members by byte range costs two requests per member, which
exhausts Dryad's daily request limit on corpus runs. .zip_fetch_members()
gains a whole-archive mode: when at least 3 members are wanted and the
archive (size estimated from its central directory) fits the budget, it
downloads the archive once, keeps it on disk for restarted runs, and
extracts the wanted members locally; anything not delivered falls back to
the per-member fetch. Enabled only for datadryad.org archives, in
download_repo_files() and code_check's zip expansion. Version 0.3.2.2.

recent_commits.message: Add Python support to reproducibility_check
recent_commits.body:
Extends the module to assess and (optionally) execute Python code
alongside R, mirroring the existing R pipeline's static analysis,
execution, and reporting:

- code_file_refs()/code_library_names() (R/code_check.R): Python write-
  call detection (to_csv/savefig/np.save/pickle.dump/...), alongside the
  existing Python read/import support.
- repro_file_io()/repro_rewrite_paths()/repro_write_scripts()
  (R/reproducibility_check.R): now accept lang = "Python" -- read/write/
  path-rewrite detection, os.chdir() stripping (Python's setwd()
  equivalent), and a full Python port of the write-redirect logic
  (os.path.join()-aware). Font-substitution and library() injection
  stay R-only (no Python equivalent exists for either).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python.R: repro_dependencies_py()
  (import + requirements.txt/pyproject.toml parsing), a static Python
  stdlib module list, repro_install_deps_py()/repro_run_scripts_py()
  (pip/process-based execution backend, mirroring the R callr backend
  but running each script whole -- no per-statement object capture).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python_docker.R: the Docker-sandboxed
  mirror, reusing the existing generic container-lifecycle helpers
  (non-root uid, container-name/stop-on-timeout, resource limits).
- A Python corrective re-run step (reorders scripts to resolve a
  NameError to another script's top-level definition) -- confirmed via
  testing that, unlike R's shared-session corrective reorder, this can
  never actually fix a genuine Python NameError (each script runs as
  its own OS process with no shared namespace); documented as a known,
  structural limitation rather than removed.
- Python scripts' stdout now feeds the same STATO-typed "Reported vs.
  reproduced" matching R output does, via the already-existing
  .ipynb_stat_line()/.ipynb_stat_table() text parsers (built for
  Jupyter notebook cells, reused here against live execution output) --
  no new statistics-extraction code needed.
- inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R: replaces the hard R-only
  language gate with a dispatch that runs the R and Python pipelines
  in parallel and merges their table/summary_table/report/traffic_light
  into one result.

New Python test fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/repro/*.py) and unit/
module-level tests mirroring the existing R ones; Docker/interpreter-
gated tests skip cleanly when unavailable. 247 tests passing.

recent_commits.message: Add Python support to reproducibility_check
recent_commits.body:
Extends the module to assess and (optionally) execute Python code
alongside R, mirroring the existing R pipeline's static analysis,
execution, and reporting:

- code_file_refs()/code_library_names() (R/code_check.R): Python write-
  call detection (to_csv/savefig/np.save/pickle.dump/...), alongside the
  existing Python read/import support.
- repro_file_io()/repro_rewrite_paths()/repro_write_scripts()
  (R/reproducibility_check.R): now accept lang = "Python" -- read/write/
  path-rewrite detection, os.chdir() stripping (Python's setwd()
  equivalent), and a full Python port of the write-redirect logic
  (os.path.join()-aware). Font-substitution and library() injection
  stay R-only (no Python equivalent exists for either).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python.R: repro_dependencies_py()
  (import + requirements.txt/pyproject.toml parsing), a static Python
  stdlib module list, repro_install_deps_py()/repro_run_scripts_py()
  (pip/process-based execution backend, mirroring the R callr backend
  but running each script whole -- no per-statement object capture).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python_docker.R: the Docker-sandboxed
  mirror, reusing the existing generic container-lifecycle helpers
  (non-root uid, container-name/stop-on-timeout, resource limits).
- A Python corrective re-run step (reorders scripts to resolve a
  NameError to another script's top-level definition) -- confirmed via
  testing that, unlike R's shared-session corrective reorder, this can
  never actually fix a genuine Python NameError (each script runs as
  its own OS process with no shared namespace); documented as a known,
  structural limitation rather than removed.
- Python scripts' stdout now feeds the same STATO-typed "Reported vs.
  reproduced" matching R output does, via the already-existing
  .ipynb_stat_line()/.ipynb_stat_table() text parsers (built for
  Jupyter notebook cells, reused here against live execution output) --
  no new statistics-extraction code needed.
- inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R: replaces the hard R-only
  language gate with a dispatch that runs the R and Python pipelines
  in parallel and merges their table/summary_table/report/traffic_light
  into one result.

New Python test fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/repro/*.py) and unit/
module-level tests mirroring the existing R ones; Docker/interpreter-
gated tests skip cleanly when unavailable. 247 tests passing.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add Python support to reproducibility_check
recent_commits.body:
Extends the module to assess and (optionally) execute Python code
alongside R, mirroring the existing R pipeline's static analysis,
execution, and reporting:

- code_file_refs()/code_library_names() (R/code_check.R): Python write-
  call detection (to_csv/savefig/np.save/pickle.dump/...), alongside the
  existing Python read/import support.
- repro_file_io()/repro_rewrite_paths()/repro_write_scripts()
  (R/reproducibility_check.R): now accept lang = "Python" -- read/write/
  path-rewrite detection, os.chdir() stripping (Python's setwd()
  equivalent), and a full Python port of the write-redirect logic
  (os.path.join()-aware). Font-substitution and library() injection
  stay R-only (no Python equivalent exists for either).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python.R: repro_dependencies_py()
  (import + requirements.txt/pyproject.toml parsing), a static Python
  stdlib module list, repro_install_deps_py()/repro_run_scripts_py()
  (pip/process-based execution backend, mirroring the R callr backend
  but running each script whole -- no per-statement object capture).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python_docker.R: the Docker-sandboxed
  mirror, reusing the existing generic container-lifecycle helpers
  (non-root uid, container-name/stop-on-timeout, resource limits).
- A Python corrective re-run step (reorders scripts to resolve a
  NameError to another script's top-level definition) -- confirmed via
  testing that, unlike R's shared-session corrective reorder, this can
  never actually fix a genuine Python NameError (each script runs as
  its own OS process with no shared namespace); documented as a known,
  structural limitation rather than removed.
- Python scripts' stdout now feeds the same STATO-typed "Reported vs.
  reproduced" matching R output does, via the already-existing
  .ipynb_stat_line()/.ipynb_stat_table() text parsers (built for
  Jupyter notebook cells, reused here against live execution output) --
  no new statistics-extraction code needed.
- inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R: replaces the hard R-only
  language gate with a dispatch that runs the R and Python pipelines
  in parallel and merges their table/summary_table/report/traffic_light
  into one result.

New Python test fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/repro/*.py) and unit/
module-level tests mirroring the existing R ones; Docker/interpreter-
gated tests skip cleanly when unavailable. 247 tests passing.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a caption box stops where the neighbouring text column begins
recent_commits.body:
A caption in one text column shares its y-row with the other column's text, so
its box ran to the far margin; the region swallowed the neighbour's prose and was
rejected as body prose. 10.1177/01461672251327169 p15 Table 10 delivered 'Measure'
and none of its 24 values. The right edge is now the first glyph of the row's
second text block (a gap of 12pt+ overlapping the page's central band).

Measured over 101 manifest papers: 12 firings, 2 tables changed, both improved
(ip_feldman Table 10: 0 -> 40 cells, values page-verified; 10.1177/00221465251343322
Table 4: unstructured text with body prose appended -> 62-cell grid matching the page).
0 regressions.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(extract): decode Linotype Pi glyph names (/H11005 ...) in fonts with no ToUnicode
recent_commits.body:
Operators and Greek set in Linotype Pi fonts arrived as "!" "'" "&" (Linux
poppler) or U+2AFD (Windows poppler), so an APA paper's statistics could not
be parsed. docpluck/glyph_names.py adds a ToUnicode map to an in-memory copy
of the PDF from a table of raster-verified glyph names; text, layout and
Camelot read that copy. method names the repaired fonts and any H-named glyph
it could not map. rho is emitted as printed. Ordinary PDFs are byte-identical
(40 corpus papers). 2.4.150, normalization 1.9.71, table extraction 2.4.21.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Merge origin/dev into read-bibr-schema-12-1
recent_commits.body:
The bibr 12.x entries move from 0.3.1, which dev has released, to 0.3.2,
the version in progress.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Say why read() could not read a file, and keep the others
recent_commits.body:
read() logged the error of a file it could not read and returned NULL
for it, which paperlist() then rejected: the call stopped with "The
arguments must be paper objects or lists of paper objects" and the
reason, such as an unsupported bibr schema, was only in the log. It now
warns with the file's name and the reason and returns the papers it
could read, an empty paperlist when there are none.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.1 from the ScienceVerse Platform
recent_commits.body:
bibr 0.6.0 and the ScienceVerse Platform write schema 12.1, which adds
extraction.fields, the state of each tracked field. read() already reads
it: the 12.x reader keeps the extraction block whole. This adds a 12.1
export the Platform returned, of a CC BY 4.0 paper, and tests that a
citation resolves to its reference by target_id, that captions and notes
are text rows with no section, that extraction.fields says why the DOI
is missing, that a later 12.x with a new key, block and section type
reads, and that files without a root schema_version, alone or next to a
12.x file in one folder, still read in the older format.

An export in another schema now says what to do, as pytacheck does:
extract the paper again with a bibr version that writes 12.x, or, for a
newer schema, update metacheck.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Fix .figshare_id() for the 4 institutional hosts added in #464
recent_commits.body:
UCL's sub-prefix is /-separated rather than .-separated, Adelaide mints
both numeric and opaque hex-shaped DOI suffixes, and VTechData/USDA's
DOI suffixes carry no real article id at all (USDA's embedded number is
a different id entirely). Fixes #465.

recent_commits.message: Say why read() could not read a file, and keep the others
recent_commits.body:
read() logged the error of a file it could not read and returned NULL
for it, which paperlist() then rejected: the call stopped with "The
arguments must be paper objects or lists of paper objects" and the
reason, such as an unsupported bibr schema, was only in the log. It now
warns with the file's name and the reason and returns the papers it
could read, an empty paperlist when there are none.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.1 from the ScienceVerse Platform
recent_commits.body:
bibr 0.6.0 and the ScienceVerse Platform write schema 12.1, which adds
extraction.fields, the state of each tracked field. read() already reads
it: the 12.x reader keeps the extraction block whole. This adds a 12.1
export the Platform returned, of a CC BY 4.0 paper, and tests that a
citation resolves to its reference by target_id, that captions and notes
are text rows with no section, that extraction.fields says why the DOI
is missing, that a later 12.x with a new key, block and section type
reads, and that files without a root schema_version, alone or next to a
12.x file in one folder, still read in the older format.

An export in another schema now says what to do, as pytacheck does:
extract the paper again with a bibr version that writes 12.x, or, for a
newer schema, update metacheck.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

newer schema, update metacheck.
