recent_commits.message: Remove the date-format file-naming rule; relabel severity for display
recent_commits.body:
The date-format rule flagged any 8-digit run in a filename that failed to
parse as YYYYMMDD. There is no reliable way to tell, from the filename
alone, whether an 8-digit run was ever intended as a date rather than some
other numeric ID (a DOI suffix, an accession number, a participant code),
so the heuristic produced false positives with no way to avoid them (#462,
a 16-digit ID sliced into two bogus "invalid date" violations). Removed
rather than patched further.

Also relabels the naming-issues table's Severity column from the internal
"bad"/"suggestion" values to "Required"/"Suggestion" for display, without
changing the underlying severity classification or any gating logic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Redesign the brief/simple report: statement-style layout, fold findings by file, trim redundant summary lines
recent_commits.body:
The brief to-do list previously split a check's problem from its location
across separate tables/groups (e.g. "N items: Status: absent" followed by
quoted "sentences" that were actually bare file names), duplicated counts
already stated in the module summary, and always printed a confirmation
line for checks that found nothing. code_check's and repo_check's
per-finding bullets are now folded by file, naming both what was found and
where in one line, with the flagged values bolded; parse-error and other
free-text findings are collapsed to a single line instead of breaking
across the rendered table's embedded line breaks. code_check.R and
codebook_check.R drop the always-on "nothing found" / redundant headline
lines from their brief summary_text, and code_check.R's version-pin
summary adds a one-line remediation suggestion.

The simple (email-safe, static) report gets a bank-statement-style visual
redesign: a full-bleed brand-green banner with the Metacheck logo (embedded
as a base64 data URI so the report stays a single self-contained file) and
a dot-pattern texture, ledger-style summary rows with a left accent stripe
per traffic light, and restyled tables/callouts to match. Fixes several
bugs surfaced along the way: a Pandoc header-attribute id built from a
module title containing parentheses broke and leaked literal `{#id}`
syntax into the rendered heading/TOC; the brief-mode header rewrite
stripped the banner entirely since it used to cut everything after
`</style>`; and the template's own CSS pushed `sprintf()`'s format-string
past its 8192-character limit, crashing the render, so the header
templating was switched to length-safe sequential substitution.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: fix(extract): decode Linotype Pi glyph names (/H11005 ...) in fonts with no ToUnicode
recent_commits.body:
Operators and Greek set in Linotype Pi fonts arrived as "!" "'" "&" (Linux
poppler) or U+2AFD (Windows poppler), so an APA paper's statistics could not
be parsed. docpluck/glyph_names.py adds a ToUnicode map to an in-memory copy
of the PDF from a table of raster-verified glyph names; text, layout and
Camelot read that copy. method names the repaired fonts and any H-named glyph
it could not map. rho is emitted as printed. Ordinary PDFs are byte-identical
(40 corpus papers). 2.4.150, normalization 1.9.71, table extraction 2.4.21.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(harness): glyph check counts only a U+FFFD the pipeline introduced
recent_commits.body:
Since 2026-09-24 an undecodable glyph passes through as U+FFFD as the file
declares it. The check failed on ANY U+FFFD, so plos-med-1 (9 in its own text
layer, 15 in the render because the table channel re-reads the same printed
signs) regressed against a 2026-09-26 baseline on every level. A U+FFFD now
counts only if the token glued after it never follows a U+FFFD in raw.txt;
with no raw view every U+FFFD still counts. Two-sided: plos-med-1 passes, a
duplicated real glyph passes, a newly introduced one fails.

line for checks that found nothing. code_check's and repo_check's
per-finding bullets are now folded by file, naming both what was found and
where in one line, with the flagged values bolded; parse-error and other
free-text findings are collapsed to a single line instead of breaking
across the rendered table's embedded line breaks. code_check.R and
codebook_check.R drop the always-on "nothing found" / redundant headline
lines from their brief summary_text, and code_check.R's version-pin
summary adds a one-line remediation suggestion.

The simple (email-safe, static) report gets a bank-statement-style visual
redesign: a full-bleed brand-green banner with the Metacheck logo (embedded
as a base64 data URI so the report stays a single self-contained file) and
a dot-pattern texture, ledger-style summary rows with a left accent stripe
per traffic light, and restyled tables/callouts to match. Fixes several
bugs surfaced along the way: a Pandoc header-attribute id built from a
module title containing parentheses broke and leaked literal `{#id}`
syntax into the rendered heading/TOC; the brief-mode header rewrite
stripped the banner entirely since it used to cut everything after
`</style>`; and the template's own CSS pushed `sprintf()`'s format-string
past its 8192-character limit, crashing the render, so the header
templating was switched to length-safe sequential substitution.

recent_commits.message: Fix archive download promotion, extend data/code extension registry, normalize GROBID DOI whitespace (#456, #441, #411)
recent_commits.body:
A 317-paper validation audit (issues #456, #441, #411) was run against a
pinned 0.3.1 snapshot predating several fixes already on dev (the
peek_zips default mismatch, the #441 Shapefile/.gpkg additions, and the
Dryad 401 hint in download_repo_files() were all already fixed) -- this
commit addresses the remaining, still-live gaps confirmed against current
dev:

- data_check(): the archive-rescue `want` formula used an AND where a
  freshly-discovered archive (typed "unknown") needed its FALSE promoted
  to TRUE; an AND can only narrow an already-TRUE value, so every unopened
  archive under download = "data" silently never got expanded (#456.1).
- .ext_registry: added .rdat, .str, .dtg (data) and .nlogo, .jl (code),
  each confirmed against a real corpus example in #456's audit.
- import-grobid.R: GROBID's PDF-to-text extraction sometimes re-flows a
  PDF line-wrap boundary as a literal space, splitting a repository DOI
  mid-string ("https ://...", "doi. org/..."). Collapsed centrally in
  .process_full_text() rather than per-regex in each archive-*.R backend
  (#411 bug 2).
- archive-dryad.R: factored the standalone dryad_file_download() export's
  per-file byte fetch into .dryad_download_one_file(), and gave it the
  same Dryad-401-vs-API-key-missing hint download_repo_files() already
  has, so a missing-key failure isn't indistinguishable from any other
  download problem in this less-used export either (#456.6 polish).

Left for a follow-up, since both explicitly call for a design decision
rather than a mechanical fix:
- #411 bug 1 (text_search()'s include_refs = FALSE hiding a reference-
  list-only DOI) -- needs a decision on the misattribution risk the issue
  itself raises.
- #443 (data_classify_files() Tier 2 provenance/redesign proposal) -- a
  structural redesign, not a bug fix.

Also confirmed #456.3 (.rar/.7z unsupported) is an explicitly acknowledged,
unaddressable limitation, to note when closing that item.

recent_commits.message: fix(harness): glyph check counts only a U+FFFD the pipeline introduced
recent_commits.body:
Since 2026-09-24 an undecodable glyph passes through as U+FFFD as the file
declares it. The check failed on ANY U+FFFD, so plos-med-1 (9 in its own text
layer, 15 in the render because the table channel re-reads the same printed
signs) regressed against a 2026-09-26 baseline on every level. A U+FFFD now
counts only if the token glued after it never follows a U+FFFD in raw.txt;
with no raw view every U+FFFD still counts. Two-sided: plos-med-1 passes, a
duplicated real glyph passes, a newly introduced one fails.

recent_commits.message: Throw all user-facing errors via `abort_in_export()`
recent_commits.body:
* Converted the 33 `cli::cli_abort()` calls with `call = rlang::caller_env()`
  or a `call` parameter, which blamed whatever function called the check:
  an internal helper if one was in between, or `seq_disperse()` within
  `grim_map_seq()`. Dropped the `call` parameters of
  `abort_symmetric_invalid()`, `check_comb_value()`,
  `check_decidable_n_items()`, and `recycle_length_common()`.
* Converted 17 more input checks without a `call`, which blamed themselves,
  e.g. "Error in `check_debit_inputs()`" for `debit_map()`.
* `vectorize_test()` no longer builds the wrapper's call for errors, and its
  mapper hint names `grim_map()` under `lapply()`, not `FUN_map()`.
* Left internal errors and the generic `class_with()` and `call_on()` as
  they were.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix two misattributed error messages in `reround()` and the dispersers
recent_commits.body:
* An invalid `rounding` string in `reround()` named the internal
  `reconstruct_rounded_numbers_scalar()`; it now goes through
  `abort_in_export()`.
* A non-numeric `dispersion` in `seq_disperse()` and `disperse()` failed in
  base R's `round()`; both now check its type first.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Attribute errors in mapper and factory helpers to the user-called function
recent_commits.body:
* Replaced the hard-coded frame counts of `name_caller_call(n = 2L)`,
  `(n = 3L)`, and `error_digits_flawed()`'s `rlang::caller_env(4)` by
  `name_last_export_code()` and `abort_in_export()`. Errors used to say,
  e.g., "Error in `check_factory_dots()`" and named `FUN()` under
  `lapply()`; they now name `grim_map()` either way.
* Added jarl.toml so that jarl accepts repeated bullet names in
  `abort_in_export()`, as it does for cli functions.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix #93: name the user-called function in `digits_*` errors
recent_commits.body:
* `check_newly_numeric()` and `error_digits_missing()` use
  `name_last_export()` and `index_last_export()` instead of
  `caller_test_fn()`, which matched names against a pattern and so took
  `grim_plot()` for the culprit in `grim_plot(grim_map(x))`.

  package code, so a lazily evaluated argument like `grim_map(x)` above is

recent_commits.message: fix(harness): glyph check counts only a U+FFFD the pipeline introduced
recent_commits.body:
Since 2026-09-24 an undecodable glyph passes through as U+FFFD as the file
declares it. The check failed on ANY U+FFFD, so plos-med-1 (9 in its own text
layer, 15 in the render because the table channel re-reads the same printed
signs) regressed against a 2026-09-26 baseline on every level. A U+FFFD now
counts only if the token glued after it never follows a U+FFFD in raw.txt;
with no raw view every U+FFFD still counts. Two-sided: plos-med-1 passes, a
duplicated real glyph passes, a newly introduced one fails.

recent_commits.message: Add per-module brief-mode bullet renderers, a combined validation table, and a feedback line
recent_commits.body:
Several modules' report tables mix genuine findings with unconditional
inventory in ways the generic grouping heuristic can't tell apart, so
this adds named renderers for power (filter power_type to only
"unknown"/LLM-missing rows), code_check and data_check (file/column
inventory vs. actual issues tables), repo_check (file-naming issues
vs. repository/file-manifest/classification inventory, plus a
per-repository Error), reproducibility_check (run-order/exec/match
tables filtered to non-ran_ok/non-full rows, with the real
stdout/stderr transcript surfaced as a <details> dropdown for
errored/timed-out scripts), and stat_effect_size (the missing-effect-
size sentences vs. the "all detected and assessed stats" table,
filtered to confirmed no_match rows only).

Also adds a single combined "Validation" section at the bottom of
brief/simple_brief reports (a table of every flagged module's
<validation> text, replacing the per-module callout full/simple still
carry), and a feedback/contact line reusing the full report's own
email and issues URL.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Extend GROBID DOI-whitespace fix to more safe anchors (#458)
recent_commits.body:
#411's fix only collapsed two corruption shapes (https ://..., doi.
org/...). A 50-paper re-validation found 23 papers still corrupted by
the same line-wrap artifact at a different position. This adds more
anchors with the same safety property (a fixed literal substring that
never occurs in ordinary prose): a DOI's "10.NNNN/" prefix, benefiting
every platform's bare-DOI detector, plus the single-fixed-host
literals zenodo.org/, osf.io/, and researchbox.org/ and the /dryad./
and /zenodo. suffix shapes. Resolves 10 of the 23 papers; the rest
need either line-wrap position info GROBID doesn't currently expose,
or live API disambiguation -- not a text-normalization fix.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add a brief report_type() for a fast, actionable to-do list
recent_commits.body:
report_type() gains "brief" and "simple_brief" values alongside the
existing "full"/"simple" -- an orthogonal axis (content amount vs.
rendering mechanics) that trims a report down to only flagged
modules, grouped by the specific issue found, with the actual
offending text/file quoted. Several modules (power.R, code_check.R,
data_check.R) needed their own bullet renderers rather than one
fully generic heuristic, since what counts as "an issue" vs. normal
output varies per module in ways no shared column convention
captures.

Also redesigns the plain/email-safe template's CSS (the old
"margin-left: -20px" rule had nothing to push against on a
Bootstrap-free page, running headings off-screen), adds a
"How It Works" link to each module's online manual chapter, and adds
data-raw/report-all-types.R to render all four report types from one
module run for comparison.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix archive download promotion, extend data/code extension registry, normalize GROBID DOI whitespace (#456, #441, #411)
recent_commits.body:
A 317-paper validation audit (issues #456, #441, #411) was run against a
pinned 0.3.1 snapshot predating several fixes already on dev (the
peek_zips default mismatch, the #441 Shapefile/.gpkg additions, and the
Dryad 401 hint in download_repo_files() were all already fixed) -- this
commit addresses the remaining, still-live gaps confirmed against current
dev:

- data_check(): the archive-rescue `want` formula used an AND where a
  freshly-discovered archive (typed "unknown") needed its FALSE promoted
  to TRUE; an AND can only narrow an already-TRUE value, so every unopened
  archive under download = "data" silently never got expanded (#456.1).
- .ext_registry: added .rdat, .str, .dtg (data) and .nlogo, .jl (code),
  each confirmed against a real corpus example in #456's audit.
- import-grobid.R: GROBID's PDF-to-text extraction sometimes re-flows a
  PDF line-wrap boundary as a literal space, splitting a repository DOI
  mid-string ("https ://...", "doi. org/..."). Collapsed centrally in
  .process_full_text() rather than per-regex in each archive-*.R backend
  (#411 bug 2).
- archive-dryad.R: factored the standalone dryad_file_download() export's
  per-file byte fetch into .dryad_download_one_file(), and gave it the
  same Dryad-401-vs-API-key-missing hint download_repo_files() already
  has, so a missing-key failure isn't indistinguishable from any other
  download problem in this less-used export either (#456.6 polish).

Left for a follow-up, since both explicitly call for a design decision
rather than a mechanical fix:
- #411 bug 1 (text_search()'s include_refs = FALSE hiding a reference-
  list-only DOI) -- needs a decision on the misattribution risk the issue
  itself raises.
- #443 (data_classify_files() Tier 2 provenance/redesign proposal) -- a
  structural redesign, not a bug fix.

Also confirmed #456.3 (.rar/.7z unsupported) is an explicitly acknowledged,
unaddressable limitation, to note when closing that item.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix archive download promotion, extend data/code extension registry, normalize GROBID DOI whitespace (#456, #441, #411)
recent_commits.body:
A 317-paper validation audit (issues #456, #441, #411) was run against a
pinned 0.3.1 snapshot predating several fixes already on dev (the
peek_zips default mismatch, the #441 Shapefile/.gpkg additions, and the
Dryad 401 hint in download_repo_files() were all already fixed) -- this
commit addresses the remaining, still-live gaps confirmed against current
dev:

- data_check(): the archive-rescue `want` formula used an AND where a
  freshly-discovered archive (typed "unknown") needed its FALSE promoted
  to TRUE; an AND can only narrow an already-TRUE value, so every unopened
  archive under download = "data" silently never got expanded (#456.1).
- .ext_registry: added .rdat, .str, .dtg (data) and .nlogo, .jl (code),
  each confirmed against a real corpus example in #456's audit.
- import-grobid.R: GROBID's PDF-to-text extraction sometimes re-flows a
  PDF line-wrap boundary as a literal space, splitting a repository DOI
  mid-string ("https ://...", "doi. org/..."). Collapsed centrally in
  .process_full_text() rather than per-regex in each archive-*.R backend
  (#411 bug 2).
- archive-dryad.R: factored the standalone dryad_file_download() export's
  per-file byte fetch into .dryad_download_one_file(), and gave it the
  same Dryad-401-vs-API-key-missing hint download_repo_files() already
  has, so a missing-key failure isn't indistinguishable from any other
  download problem in this less-used export either (#456.6 polish).

Left for a follow-up, since both explicitly call for a design decision
rather than a mechanical fix:
- #411 bug 1 (text_search()'s include_refs = FALSE hiding a reference-
  list-only DOI) -- needs a decision on the misattribution risk the issue
  itself raises.
- #443 (data_classify_files() Tier 2 provenance/redesign proposal) -- a
  structural redesign, not a bug fix.

Also confirmed #456.3 (.rar/.7z unsupported) is an explicitly acknowledged,
unaddressable limitation, to note when closing that item.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

public dataset. data_check and code_check depend on those bytes, so a
missing key silently zeroed out columns/code analysis with only a bare

recent_commits.message: fix(verify_corpus): tag C fires on a concatenated caption, not a long one
recent_commits.body:
Tag C was "longest figure caption > 800 chars", a proxy for the v2.3.0 Bug 4
leak. It false-FAILed every release since 2.4.145 on an 864-char Nature legend
that is correct against the printed page, and it read only captions whose line
starts with "*Figure" (14 of 116 figures in the 28-paper corpus).

Now: every caption line under a "### Figure N" heading is read (116 of 116);
C = a second caption start inside one caption line (FAIL); c = a caption over
800 chars with no second label (WARN, still visible). Measured on the 28
corpus renders: 0 real firings, 0 of 27 body sentences opening with a figure
reference, 92 of 92 spliced adjacent real captions caught. The new tests fail
10/10 against the old rule.

method piece as degraded only if its name ends in _failed, so the label is

recent_commits.message: fix(render): a trailing bare number moves onto the next heading only when the paper numbers its sections
recent_commits.body:

floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A
125-paper census (2026-10-01, every case checked on the rendered page,
second model concurring) found four headings manufactured that way:
a running page number (10.5334/irsp.945 "43. Discussion", 10.5334/irsp.946
"31. References"), a sentence-final reference digit pulled out of its
sentence (10.1525/collabra.57785 "...in Table" / "8. Discussion") and a
notes item number (10.1177/19485506211056761 "4. Author Contributions").

Multi-level numbers still move on shape (every one in the census was
printed with its heading); components are 1-2 digits with a non-zero first,
so a bare cell value like 0.05 never qualifies. A single-level N moves only
when the document prints a numbered subsection of N or N-1 (10.1017/
jdm.2023.15 keeps "3. Results" now that Table 1 sits between "3." and
"Results"). Census after: the four wrong headings gone, no numbered heading
lost relative to v2.4.147, the multi-level and vouched single-level
restorations kept.

recent_commits.message: Label an unmatched subscripted Hedges' g_av as indeterminate, not no_match
recent_commits.body:
d_z and d_rm(r=0.5) are fully determined by t and df alone, so a
reported value that doesn't match either really is a confirmed
inconsistency. Hedges' g_av (Cumming, 2012's bias-corrected
average-variance standardizer) also depends on the individual
condition SDs and the true observed correlation between them --
information a bare t(df) does not preserve -- so a correctly-computed
g_av can legitimately fail every tested formula without being wrong.
Reusing "no_match" for both cases made a verified-correct g_av
indistinguishable from a real reporting error.

When the reported effect size is an explicitly subscripted Hedges' g
(g_av/g_z/g_rm/gs -- not bare, unsubscripted "g", which is ambiguous
with the original Hedges, 1981 correction that IS a deterministic
multiplier of d) and matches none of the three tested formulas, label
it "indeterminate" (cannot verify) instead of "no_match" (verified and
inconsistent) -- the same distinction the module already draws for a
Welch's t-test's non-integer df.

Also normalizes parse_d_stats()'s label before checking it: without an
apostrophe ("Hedges g av" vs "Hedges' g av", as GROBID sometimes
renders it), the whole phrase is captured as one label rather than
just "g av", so a leading Hedges'/Cohen's word is stripped first (#455).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix #448 follow-up: bare "g av"/"g_av" with no Hedges'/Cohen's prefix
recent_commits.body:
The previous #448 fix only extended extract_eq()'s match when the
"Hedges'"/"Cohen's" prefix word was present before the collapsed
subscript. A bare "g av" or literal-underscore "g_av"/"d_z" (no prefix
word at all -- as can happen on a second mention or in a table cell)
still fell through to the original bug, mis-parsing "av"/"z"/etc. as
an unrelated standalone statistic.

Added a second, narrowly-scoped alternative to extract_eq()'s pattern:
a bare "g"/"d" immediately followed by one of its own known subscript
words (av/z/rm/s), gated to exactly that letter+word pairing rather
than "one extra word after any statistic name" -- the latter would
also fuse unrelated adjacent words that happen to precede a number
("sample size n = 40" -> "size n", "mean age years = 25" -> "age
years"), confirmed by testing both sentences directly.

Also extended stat_effect_size's parse_d_stats() numeric-value regex
to accept a literal underscore (not just whitespace) between the
letter and its subscript suffix, so "g_av"/"d_z" written with an
underscore -- not only GROBID's space-collapsed form -- has its value
parsed for coherence checking rather than being recognized as an
effect size but reported as unparseable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix extract_eq() dropping effect sizes when GROBID collapses a subscript
recent_commits.body:
GROBID renders a subscripted stat like Hedges' g_av as plain
space-separated text ("Hedges' g av"). extract_eq()'s "statistic name"
character class in R/text-extractors.R could only match a single word,
so the engine backtracked past the whole "Hedges' g " prefix and
matched a clean, unrelated "av = 1.76" instead -- silently discarding
both the "Hedges'" prefix and the "g" label, not just mis-filing them.
Downstream, stat_effect_size reported the effect size as not reported
at all (red), even though it was present and consistent with the test.

Allowed the statistic name to span one extra short all-letter word
immediately before the operator, but only when the Hedges'/Cohen's
prefix group actually matched -- so an unrelated adjacent clause like
"(beta = 0.74, t(260) = 11.32)" still parses as two separate
statistics rather than being fused into one.

Also extended stat_effect_size's own label_lhs() regex to recognize
the now-preserved "g av"/"g z"/"g rm" labels as effect sizes, parallel
to how it already recognizes Cohen's "d av"/"d z"/"d rm" (#448).

recent_commits.message: Fix R<4.5 paper() crash and crossref_doi()'s experimental Labs dependency
recent_commits.body:
paper() computed its random id with tools::md5sum(bytes = _), which
needs R >= 4.5.0, while DESCRIPTION allows R >= 4.3.0. read() builds
papers through paper() and swallows the error, so every read() failed
on R < 4.5 with only a misleading paperlist() message. Replaced with
digest::digest(serialize = FALSE), already a dependency and already
used the same way elsewhere in the package (#445).

crossref_doi() queried the experimental api.labs.crossref.org mirror,
which has no service guarantee, instead of the production
api.crossref.org/works/{doi} endpoint that crossref_query() already
uses and that returns the same fields. Also meant the existing
online("api.crossref.org") check did not catch a Labs-specific outage.
Moved the matching cached test fixtures from api.labs.crossref.org to
api.crossref.org accordingly (#446).

recent_commits.message: fix(render): a trailing bare number moves onto the next heading only when the paper numbers its sections
recent_commits.body:
5a6ab1f moved any trailing single-level "N." past a section's appended
floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A
125-paper census (2026-10-01, every case checked on the rendered page,
second model concurring) found four headings manufactured that way:
a running page number (10.5334/irsp.945 "43. Discussion", 10.5334/irsp.946
"31. References"), a sentence-final reference digit pulled out of its
sentence (10.1525/collabra.57785 "...in Table" / "8. Discussion") and a
notes item number (10.1177/19485506211056761 "4. Author Contributions").

Multi-level numbers still move on shape (every one in the census was
printed with its heading); components are 1-2 digits with a non-zero first,
so a bare cell value like 0.05 never qualifies. A single-level N moves only
when the document prints a numbered subsection of N or N-1 (10.1017/
jdm.2023.15 keeps "3. Results" now that Table 1 sits between "3." and
"Results"). Census after: the four wrong headings gone, no numbered heading
lost relative to v2.4.147, the multi-level and vouched single-level
restorations kept.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Fix R<4.5 paper() crash and crossref_doi()'s experimental Labs dependency
recent_commits.body:
paper() computed its random id with tools::md5sum(bytes = _), which
needs R >= 4.5.0, while DESCRIPTION allows R >= 4.3.0. read() builds
papers through paper() and swallows the error, so every read() failed
on R < 4.5 with only a misleading paperlist() message. Replaced with
digest::digest(serialize = FALSE), already a dependency and already
used the same way elsewhere in the package (#445).

crossref_doi() queried the experimental api.labs.crossref.org mirror,
which has no service guarantee, instead of the production
api.crossref.org/works/{doi} endpoint that crossref_query() already
uses and that returns the same fields. Also meant the existing
online("api.crossref.org") check did not catch a Labs-specific outage.
Moved the matching cached test fixtures from api.labs.crossref.org to
api.crossref.org accordingly (#446).

recent_commits.body: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

recent_commits.message: Pipe nested calls in tests
recent_commits.body:
* Chains start from a single object and end on the expectation, per the test style in AGENTS.md; no call nests more than two deep, and no pipeline runs inside a call that is itself a pipeline step.
* A chain fits on one line, or, if very long, breaks after every pipe. Consecutive parallel lines stay on one line with their pipes aligned; at the top level, a trailing `# fmt: skip` keeps air from undoing that.
* Replace the `_` placeholder, which needs R >= 4.3, with purrr::pluck(), mapply() with purrr::map2_lgl(), and evalq() with quote() |> eval().
* Keep the call forms that test-vectorize-test.R tests as they are, and leave Allard's reference code in test-grimmer.R verbatim.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pipe nested calls and pipeline verbs in package code
recent_commits.body:
* Calls nested more than two deep become `|>` chains that start from a single object, with a line break after each pipe.
* dplyr verbs and other pipeline functions are applied through the pipe.
* Tail return() calls are gone; return() is only used for early returns.
* Roxygen examples and vignette chunks follow the same rules.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop leading dots from internal variable names
recent_commits.body:
* Arguments of functions that also take `...` keep their dots, as they guard against clashes with it: those of function_map*(), seq_*_df(), and the functions the two proto factories return.
* The proto factories themselves lose the dotted copies of the formals of the functions they return, which read them from the enclosing environment instead.
* function_map() reserves the renamed locals that could shadow arguments of `.fun`.
* Drop a tail return() in function_map_total_n_proto() and a test helper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the string `"NA"` as missing in `restore_zeros()`
recent_commits.body:

  out a missing one and became `NA` either way.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:

  negative `n` a negative count. Both now error via `check_positive()`,
  which lets missing values through.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep `unlist()` from coercing list elements in `is_numeric_like()`
recent_commits.body:
* A logical element next to a number became that number, and a factor
  its integer codes, so `list(TRUE, 1)` and `list(1, factor("a"))` were
  numeric-like. A logical value now makes a list `FALSE`, as it does a
  vector, and a factor is tested as its label.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give 0-row `audit_seq()` output the usual columns
recent_commits.body:
* `*_map_seq()` output records the dispersed variables as the `var`
  element of its `"scrutiny"` attribute. Without rows, `audit_seq()`
  can't read them off the `var` column, and it used to return only
  `hits_total` next to the reconstructed values.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Skip undecidable cases in `*_map_seq()` with `include_consistent`
recent_commits.body:
* A case with a missing key value has no verdict and nothing to disperse
  from. The default path dropped it along with the consistent cases, but
  `include_consistent = TRUE` kept it, and `seq_disperse()` then failed
  on the missing value.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep existing names of a matrix in `row_to_colnames()`
recent_commits.body:
* The name repair replaced every column name with a placeholder, not
  only the missing ones. A column whose header cells are all `NA` keeps
  its current name, so a named matrix lost that name to `V1`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't count unused factor levels in `duplicate_count()`
recent_commits.body:
* `table()` counts every level of a factor, so unused levels came out
  with a frequency of 0. Keeping only positive frequencies fixes that and
  also covers the ignored values, which the old filter removed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject an infinite `denominator`; unlist lists in `is_numeric_like()`
recent_commits.body:
* Both fraction functions share `check_denominator()`, which also rules
  out `Inf`, where `reround_to_fraction()` returned `NaN`.
* `is_numeric_like()` tests a list like the atomic vector of its
  elements, so a logical element is no longer read as a number.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove a zero-row branch misplaced into `audit_total_n()`
recent_commits.body:

  called `reverse_map_seq()` on total-n output, which fails.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(render): a trailing bare number moves onto the next heading only when the paper numbers its sections
recent_commits.body:

floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A

so a bare cell value like 0.05 never qualifies. A single-level N moves only

recent_commits.message: fix(tables,render): keep the column labels a caption used to swallow; a float never splits a heading number from its title
recent_commits.body:
Two regressions the full suite found in this branch:

- Header labels deleted. flatten recovers blank column roles from statistic
  labels that leaked into the caption (10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 8
  '... Explicit Learning F p'). 3c8b475 stopped the leak, so when the grid had
  also missed its header row the printed labels reached no field. New Table
  field header_text_below_caption: exactly the span the caption no longer
  absorbs (old trim end vs new), reduced to its leading run of statistic labels
  in flatten's own vocabulary. flatten reads caption + this field, i.e. the
  same input it had before. collabra.90203: T8 'F p', T9 'df F p BF01 95% CI',
  every other table None.
- Heading split. The ligature fix in _locate_caption_anchor lets figures whose
  caption carries a ligature anchor in the body; on 10.1017/jdm.2022.2 Figure 2
  was appended after a section body ending in the next heading's orphan '5.4.',
  so '5.4. Discussion' was no longer rejoined. A trailing bare section number
  now moves after the section's appended floats (nothing removed).

Both tests (test_tables_flatten_blank_header_recovery, orphan multilevel)
fail without these changes and pass with them.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): review fixes -- flatten reads the DOCX declaration from the cells; caption walk robust to raised glyphs and wide spacing
recent_commits.body:
From a tier-2 cross-model review (Sonnet, 2026-09-28) of this branch:

- flatten._declared_header_rows read Table['header_rows'] as the author's
  ceiling. Since 4737846 that field is the POST-fold thead count, so a folded
  second header row went into the body: reproduced on 9 of 415 tables across 66
  real DOCX manuscripts. The declaration is now rebuilt from the cells' is_header
  flags exactly as docx_tables._header_row_count built it; DOCX flatten output
  is identical to v2.4.147 on all 415 tables.
- sync_header_rows: a table with no html and no cells now reports None, not the
  capture path's leftover 1; extract_tables_docx (public) syncs too.
- _column_lines: overlap judged against the smaller of glyph and line height,
  so a raised superscript that opens a line still admits its line's glyphs.
- _caption_text_from_column: lines above the caption are skipped by vertical
  centre (a raised glyph no longer drops the first caption line); the blank
  band is now > 1.2 line heights AND > 1.5x the caption's own smallest gap, so
  double-spaced captions are not cut after one line.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a blank gap right after a bare label does not end the caption
recent_commits.body:
The blank-band stop (previous commit) ended 10.15626/mp.2022.3108 p7 Table 3
after its label, printed alone on its line above a gap and the title. The
rebuild then returned nothing and the text channel interleaved the neighbouring
column: 'Table 3 Table 4 Study stimuli ...'. The stop now skips a gap that
follows label-only text. Found by re-running the caption census; the test fails
without the exemption.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a column-rebuilt caption ends at a blank band it measures itself
recent_commits.body:
The line grouping in 3c8b475 yields only lines with chars in the caption's own
column, so the old 'blank band' stop -- which fired only when the OTHER page
column printed a line inside the gap -- could no longer fire. On
10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901 p5 Table 2 the caption then ran on into its header
row ('... for datasets used Class Class Class Class'). A gap of more than 60%
of a line height between consecutive caption lines now ends the caption.

Found by the 125-paper caption census (v2.4.147 vs branch); the test fails
without this change and passes with it.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): header_rows states the header split the table's own html used
recent_commits.body:
Each capture path wrote its own guess: Camelot hardcoded 1, the layout path
'1 if any is_header else 0', the DOCX path 'n_header or 1'. The html's <thead>
(and flatten_table, which agrees with it) often used a different number: on
10.1525/collabra.90203 6 of 12 tables disagreed (Table 5: field 0, thead 3).
The field is now set from the html at both structured-extraction exits by
tables.render.sync_header_rows: <thead> row count, 0 when the html has no
header, None when there is no grid. Documented in docs/README.md and on the
Table type.

On the DOCX path flatten._declared_header_rows reads this field as the
author's ceiling; the synced value already had that ceiling applied, so
feeding it back gives the same split.

Owner decision 2026-09-28 (d-756293): make the field honest rather than
document the old guesses. Public field change -> consumer notice.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a table caption stops at its own header row; ligatures and symbol-font glyphs no longer break its anchor
recent_commits.body:
Three causes of one symptom -- caption text that is not the printed caption,
and the table it labels exiled to 'Tables (unlocated in body)':

- A lone statistic symbol on its own line (p, t, d, n, df, or a Greek-led
  symbol such as eta-p2) was read as a wrapped title word because it is
  lowercase, so the cell-run cut never fired. 10.1525/collabra.90203 p12
  Table 8 caption ended '... Explicit Learning F p'.
- The column caption rebuild grouped chars into lines by round(top); a
  symbol-font glyph sits a point or two off its line and became a line of its
  own. 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2016.06.001 p4 Table 1 came out as
  'Table 1 alpha Summary ... Cronbach's for ... HKSS. alpha' (the second alpha
  is the header row's). Lines are now grouped by vertical overlap, in one
  helper shared by the caption and column-body walks; a line-end hyphen is
  kept and the break dropped, the library's H1 convention.
- _locate_caption_anchor compared a caption still carrying U+FB01 against the
  normalized body; it now decomposes ligatures with the same function
  normalize used on the body (Hurst Tables 4 and 6).

Hurst: 3 of 6 tables were in the appendix, now 0. Two-sided: 12 new checks
fail on 05fb622 and pass here; 191 existing caption/anchor tests pass.

recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
recent_commits.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
recent_commits.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
recent_commits.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove remnants of string key values
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.
* Drop `as.numeric()` calls and `x_orig` copies on key values that
  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`
recent_commits.body:
* They coerced `x` with `as.numeric()`, so `grim_total("5.19", 20, 2)`
  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`
  still gives `NA`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
recent_commits.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

* Only a compound first argument such as `list()`, `c()`, or
  `tibble::tibble()` still starts a chain as a call. `expect_snapshot()`
  code is unchanged.

* Extracting from a call's result is a step of the chain:
  `purrr::pluck()` for names and positions, `head()` for slices.

* Add the internal `call_on()` for steps that are an operator or an
  anonymous function, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x %% 1 == 0)`. It also covers
  `formals(f)$name`, since `purrr::pluck()` rejects pairlists.

* The suite passes with the same 19,570 expectations as before.

recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

recent_commits.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
recent_commits.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
recent_commits.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
recent_commits.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove remnants of string key values
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.
* Drop `as.numeric()` calls and `x_orig` copies on key values that
  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`
recent_commits.body:
* They coerced `x` with `as.numeric()`, so `grim_total("5.19", 20, 2)`
  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`
  still gives `NA`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
recent_commits.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

* Only a compound first argument such as `list()`, `c()`, or
  `tibble::tibble()` still starts a chain as a call. `expect_snapshot()`
  code is unchanged.

* Extracting from a call's result is a step of the chain:
  `purrr::pluck()` for names and positions, `head()` for slices.

* Add the internal `call_on()` for steps that are an operator or an
  anonymous function, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x %% 1 == 0)`. It also covers
  `formals(f)$name`, since `purrr::pluck()` rejects pairlists.

* The suite passes with the same 19,570 expectations as before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix DSpace7/DataONE metadata-and-file gaps and Figshare collection-DOI routing
recent_commits.body:
DSpace7 file listings never surfaced doi/license into repo_metadata
(archive-dspace7.R had no equivalent to legacy DSpace's attribute
mechanism). DataONE records whose EML lists a file as a bare

fine. A Figshare collection DOI (10.6084/m9.figshare.c.<id>) was
misrouted through Dataverse because dataverse.no's DOI-prefix list
wrongly included 10.6084, Figshare's own globally-registered prefix,
and even once routed correctly had no id-extraction pattern of its
own.

Fixes scienceverse/metacheck#434, scienceverse/metacheck#435.

recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix repo_check misses for 4TU, Dataverse, Figshare, DSpace7, and DataONE
recent_commits.body:
4TU (#431): .researchdata4tu_id() extracted a DOI-embedded uuid and passed
it straight to v2/articles/<id>, but the API needs a different numeric id
only a live DOI redirect reveals. Added .researchdata4tu_resolve_uuid() to
follow that redirect before querying.

Dataverse (#432): .dataverse_host_from_doi() returned the first host sharing
an ambiguous DOI prefix, picking the wrong DANS Data Station for a shared
prefix (10.17026, used by 4 separate installations). Now resolves via live
DOI redirect when a prefix maps to more than one host; also added the
missing phys-techsciences.datastations.nl prefix entry.

Figshare (#434): added collection-URL/DOI detection
(.figshare_collection_id()/.figshare_collection_articles()), mirroring the
existing project-expansion pattern. Share-links remain correctly flagged as
unsupported (no public API resolves them).

DSpace7/DataONE (#435): dataone_links() missed KNB's real #view/doi: URL
shape and had no fallback for a bare legacy KNB docid (knb.1404.1) cited
with no DOI at all. dspace7_links() had no DOI-based detection whatsoever,
so a paper citing only a DOI (never the host string) was invisible to it --
added live DOI resolution against known DSpace7 hosts.

#433 needed no change: 10.6078 was already added to
.dryad_doi_prefixes() by an earlier commit, before the issue was filed.

All fixes verified live against each issue's reported example. No
regressions in existing archive-dataone/dataverse/dryad/figshare tests.

though the record's own metadata (title/authors/license) resolved
fine. A Figshare collection DOI (10.6084/m9.figshare.c.<id>) was
misrouted through Dataverse because dataverse.no's DOI-prefix list
wrongly included 10.6084, Figshare's own globally-registered prefix,
and even once routed correctly had no id-extraction pattern of its
own.

recent_commits.message: Fix repo_check misses for 4TU, Dataverse, Figshare, DSpace7, and DataONE
recent_commits.body:
4TU (#431): .researchdata4tu_id() extracted a DOI-embedded uuid and passed
it straight to v2/articles/<id>, but the API needs a different numeric id
only a live DOI redirect reveals. Added .researchdata4tu_resolve_uuid() to
follow that redirect before querying.

Dataverse (#432): .dataverse_host_from_doi() returned the first host sharing
an ambiguous DOI prefix, picking the wrong DANS Data Station for a shared
prefix (10.17026, used by 4 separate installations). Now resolves via live
DOI redirect when a prefix maps to more than one host; also added the
missing phys-techsciences.datastations.nl prefix entry.

Figshare (#434): added collection-URL/DOI detection
(.figshare_collection_id()/.figshare_collection_articles()), mirroring the
existing project-expansion pattern. Share-links remain correctly flagged as
unsupported (no public API resolves them).

DSpace7/DataONE (#435): dataone_links() missed KNB's real #view/doi: URL
shape and had no fallback for a bare legacy KNB docid (knb.1404.1) cited
with no DOI at all. dspace7_links() had no DOI-based detection whatsoever,
so a paper citing only a DOI (never the host string) was invisible to it --
added live DOI resolution against known DSpace7 hosts.

#433 needed no change: 10.6078 was already added to
.dryad_doi_prefixes() by an earlier commit, before the issue was filed.

All fixes verified live against each issue's reported example. No
regressions in existing archive-dataone/dataverse/dryad/figshare tests.
